summary: Created from a user request: two conversions on the image-mode canvas context menu, mask -> paint and paint -> mask, each gated on the layer it needs. Filed under the MPI-424 canvas tool family. Insertion point, existing gating predicates, the undo recipe and three open product questions with assumed defaults are in brief.md.

Filed under the MPI-440 canvas-family umbrella #2 (mask and paint parity). Order, standing constraints and the shared alpha-vs-luminance decision are in tasks/MPI-440/brief.md - read it before starting this card.

Next MPI-440 member, unblocked - the user answered the two open product questions: mask to paint fills the Paint tool's CURRENT COLOUR FLAT (carrying the mask's own alpha was declined), and a conversion is a COPY, so the source layer survives and the conversion MERGES into the destination rather than replacing it. The third question needed no answer: the alpha-at-128 cut was settled by MPI-436 for the whole set.

BUILT, awaiting the user's in-app pass. Both conversions live on the image context menu through el.maskToPaint / el.paintToMask; the pixels live on the managers and the Block touches no canvas. ONE shared cut - alphaStencil() in maskUtils.js, alpha at 128, inherited from MPI-436 and not re-decided. Verified by pixel probe in Chromium, not a DOM click: mask to paint fills the current colour flat and leaves the mask and the old paint alone, paint to mask lands in manualCanvas with the region punched out of subtract, both Ctrl+Z back exactly, and an empty source returns false with NO undo entry. The source scribble was 101010 dark, which doubles as the luminance-vs-alpha proof. 429/429 tests including a new tests/layer-convert.test.cjs.
User confirmed both conversions verified in the app; final completion approved 2026-08-05.
